Solver Interface API

Solve Entry Point

The primary entry point for all solvers:

sol = solve(game, solver; warmstart=nothing, verbose=false, check_compatibility=true)
  • warmstart — a previous GNEPSolution or a WarmstartData.
  • verbose — passed to the solver; it is an argument of solve, not a field of the solver structs.
  • check_compatibility — compare required_capabilities(game) with solver_capabilities(typeof(solver)) and @warn on a mismatch. A warning does not stop the solve.

GameSolver is the abstract supertype of all solvers; WarmstartData is documented in the Solutions API.

DifferentialGamesBase.solve — Method
solve(game::GameProblem, solver::GameSolver; kwargs...) -> AbstractSolution{T}

Solve a differential game for Nash equilibrium.

Keyword Arguments

  • warmstart = nothing : Previous solution or WarmstartData
  • verbose::Bool = false : Print iteration info
  • check_compatibility = true : Warn if solver may not support game type

Returns

AbstractSolution{T} — typically GNEPSolution{T} for forward games.

source
solve(game::AbstractGameProblem, solver::GameSolver; kwargs...) -> AbstractSolution

General dispatch entry point for game types beyond GameProblem (e.g. LexicographicGameProblem, ConvexGameProblem). Solver packages implement _solve(game::ConcreteType, solver::ConcreteSolver, warmstart, verbose).

source
DifferentialGamesBase.solve — Method
solve(game::AbstractGameProblem, solver::GameSolver; kwargs...) -> AbstractSolution

General dispatch entry point for game types beyond GameProblem (e.g. LexicographicGameProblem, ConvexGameProblem). Solver packages implement _solve(game::ConcreteType, solver::ConcreteSolver, warmstart, verbose).

source
DifferentialGamesBase.solver_capabilities — Function
solver_capabilities(::Type{<:GameSolver}) -> Vector{Symbol}

Return symbols describing what problem types this solver handles. Must be a subset of CANONICAL_CAPABILITIES — see that constant for the full closed vocabulary (covers every symbol emitted by solvers in DifferentialGamesBaseSolvers.jl today, plus the Phase 0 problem-type additions).

source
DifferentialGamesBase.required_capabilities — Function
required_capabilities(game::GameProblem) -> Vector{Symbol}

Extract required solver capabilities from game structure.

source
required_capabilities(game::AbstractGameProblem) -> Vector{Symbol}

Generic fallback for problem types without a specific method (e.g. LexicographicGameProblem, ConvexGameProblem, InverseGameProblem, RecedingHorizonNashProblem). Returns an empty vector — "unknown, don't warn" — rather than erroring, so solve's capability check degrades gracefully instead of MethodErroring.

source
DifferentialGamesBase.CANONICAL_CAPABILITIES — Constant
CANONICAL_CAPABILITIES

The closed set of capability symbols solver_capabilities/required_capabilities may use. validate_capabilities checks membership; use it in tests to keep new solvers/problem types from silently drifting into an ad hoc vocabulary.

source

Dispatch Structure

solve(game::GameProblem, solver::GameSolver; ...) checks capabilities and then calls

_solve(game, solver, warmstart::Union{Nothing,WarmstartData}, verbose::Bool)

Solver packages only implement _solve (plus solver_capabilities); they do not add methods to solve. For problem types other than GameProblem (LexicographicGameProblem, ConvexGameProblem, InverseGameProblem, …) a second solve(::AbstractGameProblem, ::GameSolver) method forwards to _solve without the capability check.

Implementing a Custom Solver

A minimal solver subtypes GameSolver, declares its capabilities from the closed vocabulary CANONICAL_CAPABILITIES, and implements _solve:

using DifferentialGames, LinearAlgebra
import DifferentialGamesBase: _solve, solver_capabilities

# A trivial "solver": zero controls for every player (not a Nash equilibrium!),
# used only to show the plumbing.
struct ZeroControlSolver <: GameSolver end

solver_capabilities(::Type{ZeroControlSolver}) = [:LQGame, :DiscreteTime, :UnconstrainedGame]

function _solve(game::GameProblem{T}, ::ZeroControlSolver,
                warmstart::Union{Nothing, GNEPSolution, WarmstartData},
                verbose::Bool) where {T}
    N  = n_steps(game)
    n  = state_dim(game)
    X  = zeros(T, n, N + 1)
    X[:, 1] .= game.initial_state
    A  = game.dynamics.A isa Vector ? game.dynamics.A[1] : game.dynamics.A
    for k in 1:N
        X[:, k+1] = A * X[:, k]
    end
    times = collect(range(zero(T), step = T(game.time_horizon.dt), length = N + 1))
    trajs = [Trajectory{T}(obj.player_id, X, zeros(T, control_dim(game, obj.player_id), N),
                           times, zero(T)) for obj in game.objectives]
    return GNEPSolution{T}(game, trajs, X, nothing, :Unknown, true, 0, 0.0, Dict{Symbol,Any}())
end

game = LQGameProblem(Matrix(0.9I(2)), [Matrix(1.0I(2))[:, 1:1], Matrix(1.0I(2))[:, 2:2]],
                     [Matrix(1.0I(2)), Matrix(1.0I(2))], [fill(0.1,1,1), fill(0.1,1,1)],
                     [Matrix(1.0I(2)), Matrix(1.0I(2))], [1.0, 1.0], 1.0; dt=0.1)
sol = solve(game, ZeroControlSolver())
sol.equilibrium_type
:Unknown
Annotate `warmstart` exactly

The fallback _solve(::GameProblem, ::GameSolver, ::Union{Nothing,GNEPSolution,WarmstartData}, ::Bool) in DifferentialGamesBase is more specific in the warmstart argument than an unannotated method. Leaving warmstart untyped makes your method ambiguous with it (MethodError: _solve(...) is ambiguous). Copy the Union annotation as above.

A full guide (registering with the solver catalog, tests, external packages) is planned in the extension guide.
